note: SYNTHETIC. #187's amended criterion 5 kept the corpus in the repo because the battery it was measured against was lost (#172). The prose here is invented for this public repo -- no captured answer text -- but each case is one documented branch of `strip_dates_and_names`, and the assertion is the exact surviving token list. `kind` records intent: 'strip' means the case exists because a date or name term is removed, 'keep' because a figure must survive.

cases.prose: On 2026-08-21 you logged 42 jog minutes.
cases.why: A full ISO date locates a point in time; only the 42 is a claim.

cases.prose: The 2026-04 quarter averaged 38.5 jog minutes a week.
cases.why: The bare year-month form, without which the label shreds into 2026 and -04.

cases.prose: Aug 21 was the longest session at 6.2 miles.
cases.why: Month plus day is a calendar reference.

cases.prose: Jul 9, 2026 was the first of 12 planned tempo sessions.
cases.why: The optional year must not leave 2026 behind as a figure.

cases.prose: July 2026 totalled 214 jog minutes.
cases.why: The month-year alternative is tried first; the day form would match 'July 20' and leave the token 26.

cases.prose: July 6-13 you averaged 48.9 minutes a session.
cases.why: A day range in the first element is a date, not a measured range.

cases.prose: You fell asleep at 11:41 PM and slept 7.4 hours.
cases.why: A 12-hour clock time with AM/PM is a time of day.

cases.prose: The rest of the block (Aug 19, 21, 22, 23) recorded walking only.
cases.why: #187: a comma-separated day list that terminates cleanly is one date.

cases.prose: The walking-only days were Aug 19, 21 and 23.
cases.why: 'and' is a separator and a sentence-final period terminates the run.

cases.prose: Zone 2 work made up 63 of those minutes.
cases.why: Zone 2 is a name from the plan's heart-rate model.

cases.prose: Your 5k pace held at 9.4 min/mi.
cases.why: 5k and 10k are race distances, not counts.

cases.prose: Week 7 closed with 3 hard sessions.
cases.why: A capitalised Week label is an authored plan ordinal.

cases.prose: You rated sleep 3 out of 5 and energy 4 out of 5.
cases.why: #217: the denominator is a constant of the check-in scale; the numerator stays graded.

cases.prose: Readiness scored 82 out of 100 this morning.
cases.why: The readiness composite is the other of the two published scales.

cases.prose: You weighed 84.2kg at the last weigh-in.
cases.why: Units are open-ended, so a digit followed by letters stays a figure.

cases.prose: Your easy lane is 14-15 min/mi.
cases.why: A hyphen between measurements is a range; both ends stay graded and neither is folded into a negative.

cases.prose: You held 7:30 per mile through the final rep.
cases.why: A bare mm:ss is a pace or a duration; only a marked 12-hour clock is stripped.

cases.prose: Your VO2max estimate is 48.3.
cases.why: The leading guard keeps the 2 of VO2max out while the real figure stays.

cases.prose: Your A1c reading was 5.2 this quarter.
cases.why: Same guard, a different name.

cases.prose: This week 3 sessions are logged.
cases.why: The Week label is case-sensitive on purpose: the determiner phrase must not strip a real count.

cases.prose: On Aug 19, 44 jog minutes were recorded.
cases.why: 44 is not a day, so the continuation tail cannot eat it.

cases.prose: On Aug 19, 44.0 minutes of that were jogging.
cases.why: A decimal disqualifies a continuation element; half-eating a figure would fabricate a different number.

cases.prose: On Aug 19, 12,500 steps were recorded.
cases.why: A thousands separator disqualifies it for the same reason.

cases.prose: Aug 19, 21 and 22 were rest days.
cases.why: A run followed by a word is not a date list; a bare day left graded is the tolerable failure.

cases.prose: Since Aug 19, 8, 9, 12 were your resting HR readings
cases.why: The atomic run cannot succeed partially: the trailing word protects the interior elements too. The trailing comma rides along in the token because the tokenizer treats it as a thousands separator; `_rule_r_matches` strips it before comparing.

cases.prose: Aug 19, 21-23 were travel days.
cases.why: A range as a continuation element is deliberately not supported.

cases.prose: 3 out of 5 planned sessions were completed.
cases.why: No rating anchor, so the denominator is a genuine published count.

cases.prose: You scored 3 out of 500 on the composite.
cases.why: Only the two published constants are blanked; any other value stays graded.

cases.prose: You slept 5 h.
cases.why: The pattern strips a denominator slot, never a digit.

cases.prose: Your weight trend is -0.4 lb per week.
cases.why: A minus sign is part of the figure and must reach the gate.

cases.prose: Recovery walks ran 29-30 minutes.
cases.why: Removing the separator would fabricate 2930.

cases.prose: Jog volume rose 12.5% over the block.
cases.why: A percentage is a measurement.
